surprises.description: Werner guided only to modest sequential EPS improvement from $0.16 in Q4, well below the preview’s $0.47 consensus and also below its own $0.25–$0.35 guide estimate. The company said fuel and reserve headwinds should largely abate, but lower equipment gains, higher interest expense, and tax normalization would offset that relief.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to modest sequential EPS improvement in Q4 over the $0.16 base,” with fuel and reserve headwinds largely abating but offset by “sequentially lower equipment gains, higher interest expense, and tax normalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4'26 consensus” adj. EPS was “$0.47”; the preview said, “I'd underwrite a Q4 guide of $0.25–$0.35.”

surprises.description: One-Way produced a much stronger improvement in revenue per truck and profitability than the preview’s rate-focused outlook suggested: revenue per truck per week rose 34% and the segment turned profitable as its margin expanded by more than 800 basis points. The preview expected revenue per mile growth of 10–13%, but did not anticipate the much larger per-truck gain driven by both mileage and rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One-Way revenue per truck per week surged 34% year-over-year,” driven by “a 22% rise in miles per truck and 10% higher revenue per total mile,” while adjusted operating margin expanded “over 800 basis points, turning the segment from a loss to a profit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “One-Way revenue per mile +10–13% YoY” as a Q3 segment checkable.

surprises.description: Dedicated revenue excluding fuel surcharges grew 52% year over year, alongside a 46% increase in trucks since year-end. That was much stronger reported growth than the preview’s cited Dedicated expectation of 3–5% RPTPW growth, although the measures are not directly comparable and the fleet expansion contributed to revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dedicated revenue excluding fuel surcharges rose 52% year-over-year”; the fleet was up “2,240 trucks (46%) since year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Dedicated RPTPW +3–5%” among the segment checkables.

surprises.description: Werner lowered its full-year net CapEx outlook, which should mean less cash committed to equipment purchases than the preview expected. The reduction was attributed to OEM delivery timing rather than a change in demand or investment plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net CapEx guidance was lowered to $190-$205 million (from $215-$250 million) due to OEM delivery timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “net capex $215–250M” as the Q3 segment checkable.

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year equipment-sale gains outlook above the preview’s expected range. This provides more support to earnings from equipment gains, even as management said sequential gains would be lower in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gains on equipment sales guidance was raised to $14-$16 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected equipment gains to be “tracking $10–14M FY.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that nearly $6 million of FirstFleet savings had been delivered over eight months, below the preview’s estimate that roughly $9 million had already been actioned. The $18 million total synergy target was unchanged, but the reported savings-to-date figure was behind that preview assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FirstFleet acquisition has delivered nearly $6 million in savings over eight months (160+ basis points of margin improvement) with $18 million in total synergies targeted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q4 bridge cited “FirstFleet synergies ($18M target; ~$9M actioned).”

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete, favorable outlook for One-Way contract repricing in early 2027: double-digit average increases, with about 60% of business repriced in the first half. The preview anticipated a stronger freight market and near-term One-Way spot opportunity, but did not flag these specific repricing increases or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects early 2027 One-Way bid repricing to average double-digit increases, with roughly 60% of One-Way business repriced in the first half of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described improving freight conditions and expected One-Way peak-season spot exposure, but gave no early-2027 bid-repricing expectation.

surprises.description: Renewed FirstFleet customers retained at a very high rate, providing a favorable portfolio-retention datapoint not specified in the preview. This supports the durability of the acquired business beyond the preview’s general expectation of FirstFleet density and synergy contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: The FirstFleet portfolio had “a 98% renewal rate on renewed portfolio.”
